meta.title: "Buy it and you won't worry": your child is sold relief from fear, not a solution | Sila Slova
meta.description: Teach your child to separate emotion from decision: to spot when tension is created first, then an "exit" is sold. Game-based critical thinking course for children aged 10–16.

hero.headline: Does your child agree just to make the unease go away?
hero.subheadline: "Buy it and you won't worry." "Do it and everything will be fine." "Otherwise it'll be bad." First the tension is created — then an "exit" is handed over right away. And your child acts to remove the uncomfortable feeling, not because it's actually needed.

media.alt: A child deciding to get rid of discomfort rather than because it's needed

pain.title: This isn't a solution — it's a way to sell through fear
pain.body:
The pattern is always the same: first they scare or unsettle you — "it'll be bad", "you'll lose out", "everyone will see". Then they immediately offer an action that supposedly removes it: "buy", "do it", "agree". The tension and the "exit" come as a pair — and that's exactly why it works.

This isn't gullibility or weakness. The child just wants the discomfort gone fast — and grabs the first thing that removes it. The decision is made through emotion ("I want it to stop being scary"), not through logic ("do I actually need this?").

The result — the child agrees or "buys" not because it's needed, but to feel calmer. And once the tension passes, it often turns out the decision wasn't theirs at all — it belonged to whoever created the tension.

social_proof.quote: My son used to grab at any "do it and it'll be fine". Now he asks first: "But do I even need this?" — and sees for himself when he's just being sold peace of mind.
social_proof.author: Elena, mum of 12-year-old Nazar

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 10–16 year olds. At this age, children are receptive to new thinking patterns and are still forming their views.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
